subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm designing a Warcraft-style jungle troll: tall, hunched, lanky frame with teal-blue skin, lower-jaw tusks, long pointed ears, a crimson mohawk, bone fetish necklace and bracers, loincloth, and tribal paint. I want to keep the module efficient yet detailed, making sure the API usage stays correct throughout.

Now I'm working out the skeleton proportions — hunched spine curving forward into a jutting head, digitigrade-style legs reaching down to the feet, and long arms with backward-bending elbows reaching low toward the ground, all sized so the limb lengths comfortably span their target distances. I'm also setting up the torso loft using the spine and hip joints to give the hunched posture its shape.

Now I'm planning the head details: a skull with a lower jaw loft carrying upward tusks, long pointed ears swept back from the skull, and a mohawk built from extruded blade shapes running along the crown and down the neck with a red gradient. For eyes, I'm placing a decal with a glowing yellow eye shape onto the skull.

For fetishes, I'm sketching a bone-and-skull necklace as a closed sweep around the chest-top with hanging rod-and-sphere bones, plus bracers, while skipping a voodoo staff since it wasn't requested; I'm also planning loincloth panels and considering feather fetishes on the mohawk. For skin, I'm layering mottled teal-green countershading with warts, a lighter belly, and tribal war-paint decals on the chest and face.

Now I'm working out feet and hands: feet get a lofted shape with spiked toes anchored at the ankle tip, while hands use a palm sphere with three clawed finger chains swept from the hand tip. I'm positioning the foot sole near ground level and defining a helper function to build ring cross-sections for the sweeps, then starting the torso loft stations along the spine with width and height values at each point.

Next I'm adding the neck as a short bone chain connecting the chest to the head joint, working out how it parents to the spine and positioning the head joint above it.

Now I'm placing the head itself—the skull as a scaled sphere, the lower jaw as a bone with its own joint and box shape, and curved ivory tusks jutting from the jaw using a bezier sweep.

Next I'm working out the nose as a hooked cone, a brow capsule, and glowing yellow eyes positioned carefully along the skull's curved surface so they sit on the face naturally. Then I start sketching the ears as a chain of points swept back and upward.

Now I'm plotting a mohawk of nine blades running along the crown, tapering their width and curving the base path down the skull toward the neck using a smooth spline through control points.

Adding the mohawk bone assignment, then building arm chains with tapering radii and hands with palm spheres and downward-curving claw-like fingers using spikes attached to the hand bone.

For the necklace, I'm placing a ring of points around the neck/chest with a leather cord sweep, dangling bone rods with sphere ends spaced around the front half, plus a central hanging skull—adjusting positions so it drapes naturally as a V-shaped loop rather than a perfect ring.

Still placing beads...

Now I'm moving on to the waist, planning two loincloth panels extruded front and back hanging from a belt around the hips.

I'm adding small skull decorations on the belt and writing a reusable skull helper that builds a jaw, eye sockets, and nose from scaled spheres, facing forward for simplicity, before moving on to bone bracers on the forearms.

Now I'm placing ivory bone spikes in a ring chain along the arm, adding tusk-like spikes on the shoulders, and hanging feather fetish bundles from the belt using card textures. Then I'm scattering small wart spheres across the torso and starting a skin paint shader that mixes colors based on surface position and normal.

Writing skin paint shader...

Skipping eye decals, I'm adding face paint onto the skull part with a forward-facing direction near the head position, and keeping the types loose to satisfy strict TS without overengineering.
